revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Rooftop Garden
revealWordProblem.text: The firm is designing a regular decagon-shaped rooftop garden bed. It decomposes into 10 congruent triangles from the center, each with a base of 3 feet and a height of 4 feet. The garden center charges $5 per square foot for soil and plants. What is the total cost to fill the garden bed?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: One triangle: A = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 sq ft. The decagon has 10 sides, so it has 10 triangles: 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Cost = 60 × $5 = $300.

conceptIntro.heading: How do we find the area of a regular polygon?
conceptIntro.intro: A regular polygon is a closed shape with straight sides where every side is the same length and every angle is the same size. We can decompose it (break it apart) into equal triangles from the center, then add up their areas.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A regular polygon splits into the same number of triangles as it has sides, so total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides).

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My hexagon has 6 equal sides. Each side is 6 feet, and each center triangle has a height of 5.2 feet.
First I find one triangle: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 5.2.
I multiply: 6 × 5.2 = 31.2, then ½ × 31.2 = 15.6 square feet.
A hexagon has 6 sides, so it has 6 equal triangles.
I multiply: 6 × 15.6 = 93.6. So the total area is 93.6 square feet.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller regular pentagon: each of its 5 triangles has base 4 cm and height 3 cm.
First find one triangle: ½ × 4 × 3. What is 4 × 3? Yes, 12, and half of 12 is 6 sq cm.
A pentagon has 5 sides, so how many triangles? Yes, 5.
Multiply: 5 × 6 = 30, so the total area is 30 square centimeters.

explore.explanation: Every regular polygon breaks into congruent triangles that meet at the center — one triangle per side. Find one triangle with ½ × base × height, then multiply by the number of triangles. Hexagon: 28 × 6 = 168. Pentagon: 12 × 5 = 60. Square: 25 × 4 = 100. Octagon: 15 × 8 = 120.
explore.explanationEs: Todo polígono regular se divide en triángulos congruentes que se unen en el centro — un triángulo por cada lado. Halla el área de un triángulo con ½ × base × altura y luego multiplica por el número de triángulos. Hexágono: 28 × 6 = 168. Pentágono: 12 × 5 = 60. Cuadrado: 25 × 4 = 100. Octágono: 15 × 8 = 120.
explore.instructionsEs: Un polígono regular se divide en triángulos congruentes que se unen en el centro. Halla el área de UN triángulo, cuenta los triángulos y multiplica para obtener el polígono entero. Las dos primeras columnas ya están hechas — completa el área total.

The hexagon (6 sides) and the octagon (8 sides) are the only ones above 5; the equilateral triangle (3), the square (4), and the pentagon (exactly 5) all belong in the '5 or fewer' group.
approaching.explanationEs: Un polígono regular se divide en un triángulo por cada lado, así que la cantidad de triángulos es simplemente el número de lados. El hexágono (6 lados) y el octágono (8 lados) son los únicos por encima de 5; el triángulo equilátero (3), el cuadrado (4) y el pentágono (exactamente 5) van en el grupo de '5 o menos'.
approaching.instructionsEs: Cada polígono regular de abajo se corta en triángulos congruentes trazando una línea desde el centro hasta cada esquina. Clasifica según cuántos triángulos forma.
hintsEs: Imagínalo: un radio desde el centro hasta cada esquina. Cada triángulo se apoya en un lado.
Eso significa que el número de triángulos siempre es igual al número de lados. Nombra los lados de cada polígono primero.
Un hexágono tiene 6 lados, así que 6 triángulos. ¿Es 6 más que 5? Colócalo y sigue con el octágono, el triángulo, el cuadrado y el pentágono.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Find the area of one triangle
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra el área de un triángulo

approaching.correctWork: An octagon has 8 sides, not 5. Total area = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft — multiply one triangle's area by the actual number of sides (triangles), not a random number.
hints: Look at Step 4. How many sides does an octagon actually have?
An octagon has 8 sides, so it has 8 triangles: Total = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft, not 5 × 6.
approaching.explanation: The area of one triangle, 6 sq ft, is right, but the final step multiplied by 5 when an octagon decomposes into 8 triangles. Multiplying by the true number of sides gives Total = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft.
approaching.explanationEs: El área de un triángulo, 6 pies cuadrados, está bien, pero el último paso multiplicó por 5 cuando un octágono se descompone en 8 triángulos. Al multiplicar por el número real de lados se obtiene un total de 8 × 6 = 48 pies cuadrados.
approaching.correctWorkEs: Un octágono tiene 8 lados, no 5. Área total = 8 × 6 = 48 pies cuadrados — multiplica el área de un triángulo por el número real de lados (triángulos), no por un número cualquiera.

onLevel.hint: Identify shapes inside; use correct formula for each; add.
hints: Each row has two blanks: the area of ONE triangle first, then the total for the whole polygon.
Column 5 uses ½ × base × height. Column 6 multiplies that answer by the Number of Triangles.
Hexagon row: compute ½ × 6 × 5.2 for one triangle, then multiply your result by 6 for the total.
onLevel.explanation: Each row is two moves: one triangle's area with ½ × base × height, then that answer times the number of triangles. The hexagon gives ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 and 6 × 15.6 = 93.6 sq ft, the pentagon 22 and 110 sq ft, the square 10 and 40 sq ft, and the octagon 9.6 and 76.8 sq ft.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada fila tiene dos movimientos: el área de un triángulo con ½ × base × altura, y luego ese resultado por el número de triángulos. El hexágono da ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 y 6 × 15.6 = 93.6 pies cuadrados; el pentágono, 22 y 110; el cuadrado, 10 y 40; y el octágono, 9.6 y 76.8 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Cada fila tiene dos espacios: primero el área de UN triángulo y luego el total del polígono completo.
La columna 5 usa ½ × base × altura. La columna 6 multiplica esa respuesta por el Número de Triángulos.
Fila del hexágono: calcula ½ × 6 × 5.2 para un triángulo y luego multiplica tu resultado por 6 para el total.

pairs.termEs: Triángulo equilátero: 3 triángulos, cada uno ½×4×3

onLevel.label: Match each polygon to its total area.
onLevel.hint: Every card is the same two moves: evaluate ½ × b × h for one triangle, then multiply by the triangle count.
hints: Each polygon card shows its triangle count and one triangle's ½ × b × h setup — the match is the TOTAL area.
Work in two steps: evaluate the ½ × b × h part, then multiply by the number of triangles named.
Hexagon card: find ½ × 6 × 5.2 for one triangle, then multiply by 6 to get the total to match.
onLevel.explanation: Each card gives one triangle's setup, so evaluate it and multiply by the triangle count: hexagon 6 × 15.6 = 93.6 sq ft, pentagon 5 × 22 = 110 sq ft, octagon 8 × 9.6 = 76.8 sq ft, square 4 × 10 = 40 sq ft, decagon 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft, and the equilateral triangle 3 × 6 = 18 sq ft.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta da el planteamiento de un triángulo, así que resuélvelo y multiplícalo por la cantidad de triángulos: hexágono 6 × 15.6 = 93.6 pies cuadrados, pentágono 5 × 22 = 110, octágono 8 × 9.6 = 76.8, cuadrado 4 × 10 = 40, decágono 10 × 6 = 60 y el triángulo equilátero 3 × 6 = 18.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada polígono con su área total.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta de polígono muestra su número de triángulos y el planteamiento ½ × b × h de un triángulo; la pareja es el área TOTAL.
Trabaja en dos pasos: evalúa la parte ½ × b × h y luego multiplica por el número de triángulos indicado.
Tarjeta del hexágono: halla ½ × 6 × 5.2 para un triángulo y luego multiplica por 6 para obtener el total que buscas.

onLevel.instructions: Find the TOTAL area of each regular polygon, then sort it against the 90 sq ft cutoff.

items.text: Pentagon: 5 triangles, base 8 ft, height 5.5 ft
items.textEs: Pentágono: 5 triángulos, base 8 ft, altura 5.5 ft

items.text: Hexagon: 6 triangles, base 6 ft, height 5.2 ft
items.textEs: Hexágono: 6 triángulos, base 6 ft, altura 5.2 ft

items.text: Octagon: 8 triangles, base 4 ft, height 4.8 ft
items.textEs: Octágono: 8 triángulos, base 4 ft, altura 4.8 ft

items.text: Square: 4 triangles, base 5 ft, height 4 ft
items.textEs: Cuadrado: 4 triángulos, base 5 ft, altura 4 ft

onLevel.hint: Two steps every time: ½ × base × height for ONE triangle, then multiply by the number of triangles.
hints: Do not sort by how many sides the polygon has — more sides does not guarantee more area.
Step 1: ½ × base × height. Step 2: multiply that by the triangle count. Then compare to 90.
Pentagon: ½ × 8 × 5.5 = 22 sq ft for one triangle, and 5 × 22 = 110 sq ft total. Is 110 at least 90? Place it, then work the rest.
onLevel.explanation: Each card needs both steps. Pentagon: 5 × (½ × 8 × 5.5) = 110 sq ft. Hexagon: 6 × (½ × 6 × 5.2) = 93.6 sq ft. Both reach 90. Octagon: 8 × (½ × 4 × 4.8) = 76.8 sq ft. Square: 4 × (½ × 5 × 4) = 40 sq ft. Both fall short — and notice the octagon has the MOST sides but not the most area, because its triangles are smaller.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta necesita los dos pasos. Pentágono: 5 × (½ × 8 × 5.5) = 110 pies cuadrados. Hexágono: 6 × (½ × 6 × 5.2) = 93.6. Ambos llegan a 90. Octágono: 8 × (½ × 4 × 4.8) = 76.8. Cuadrado: 4 × (½ × 5 × 4) = 40. Ambos quedan por debajo, y fíjate que el octágono tiene MÁS lados pero no más área, porque sus triángulos son más pequeños.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Halla el área TOTAL de cada polígono regular y luego clasifícalo según el límite de 90 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: No clasifiques por cuántos lados tiene el polígono: más lados no garantiza más área.
Paso 1: ½ × base × altura. Paso 2: multiplica eso por el número de triángulos. Luego compara con 90.
Pentágono: ½ × 8 × 5.5 = 22 pies cuadrados por triángulo, y 5 × 22 = 110 en total. ¿Es 110 al menos 90? Colócalo y sigue.

onLevel.instructions: A regular hexagon decomposes into 6 congruent triangles from its center. Each triangle has a base of 5 ft, and the whole hexagon covers 75 sq ft. Plot the height of one triangle.
onLevel.label: Find the triangle height: total area = 75 sq ft, 6 triangles, base = 5 ft
onLevel.hint: Work backward: the 75 sq ft is all 6 triangles together, and each one is ½ × 5 × h.
hints: The 75 sq ft is the WHOLE hexagon — six equal triangles share it.
Since 6 × ½ × 5 = 15, every foot of height adds 15 sq ft. So the equation is 75 = 15 × h.
Divide 75 by 15 and place your point at that height.
onLevel.explanation: All six triangles share the 75 sq ft, and each one is ½ × 5 × h, so the total is 6 × ½ × 5 × h = 15h. Solving 75 = 15h gives h = 5, so the point belongs at 5 on the number line.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los seis triángulos comparten los 75 pies cuadrados, y cada uno es ½ × 5 × h, así que el total es 6 × ½ × 5 × h = 15h. Al resolver 75 = 15h se obtiene h = 5, así que el punto va en el 5 de la recta numérica.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Find the area of one triangle
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra el área de un triángulo

onLevel.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply by ½ when finding the triangle's area. A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so Total = 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
hints: Look at Step 3. What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
A triangle's area is ½ × base × height, not just base × height. One triangle = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so the total is 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
onLevel.explanation: In the step that finds one triangle's area, the student used 6 × 4 = 24 and left out the ½. A triangle is half of the rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft and the pentagon's total is 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso que halla el área de un triángulo, el estudiante usó 6 × 4 = 24 y dejó fuera el ½. Un triángulo es la mitad del rectángulo con la misma base y altura, así que A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 pies cuadrados y el total del pentágono es 5 × 12 = 60 pies cuadrados.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó multiplicar por ½ al encontrar el área del triángulo. A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 pies cuadrados, así que Total = 5 × 12 = 60 pies cuadrados.

extending.title: Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Find area of one triangle
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra el área de un triángulo

extending.correctWork: To find total area, multiply (not add): Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m. Six equal triangles means 6 times one triangle's area.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should you use to combine 6 equal triangles?
The student added 10.75 + 6 instead of multiplying 10.75 × 6.
extending.explanation: One triangle at 10.75 sq m is correct, but the last step added the 6 instead of using it as a count. Six congruent triangles means six copies of that area, so Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m.
extending.explanationEs: Un triángulo de 10.75 metros cuadrados está bien, pero el último paso sumó el 6 en lugar de usarlo como cantidad. Seis triángulos congruentes significan seis copias de esa área, así que el total es 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 metros cuadrados.
extending.correctWorkEs: Para el área total, multiplica (no sumes): Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 m cuadrados. Seis triángulos iguales significa 6 veces el área de un triángulo.

extending.prompt: A regular hexagon and a regular pentagon both have triangles with the same base (6 ft) and the same height (5 ft). Which polygon has the greater total area? Explain why the number of sides matters.
extending.sentenceFrame: One triangle's area is ½ × ___ × ___ = ___. The hexagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The pentagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The ___ has more area because ___.
extending.hint: Identify each shape; write area formula; add results.
hints: Both polygons use identical triangles (base 6 ft, height 5 ft) — only the NUMBER of triangles differs.
Find one triangle's area with ½ × 6 × 5, then multiply by 6 for the hexagon and by 5 for the pentagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5 for one triangle. Then compare 6 copies with 5 copies and explain why the counts matter.
extending.explanation: One triangle is ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft in both polygons, so the only difference is how many copies each shape holds: the hexagon has 6 for 90 sq ft and the pentagon has 5 for 75 sq ft. The hexagon has the greater area because the number of sides is exactly the number of identical triangles you get to add.
extending.explanationEs: Un triángulo mide ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 pies cuadrados en los dos polígonos, así que la única diferencia es cuántas copias tiene cada figura: el hexágono tiene 6 para 90 pies cuadrados y el pentágono tiene 5 para 75. El hexágono tiene mayor área porque el número de lados es exactamente la cantidad de triángulos iguales que puedes sumar.
extending.promptEs: Un hexágono regular y un pentágono regular tienen triángulos con la misma base (6 pies) y la misma altura (5 pies). ¿Cuál polígono tiene mayor área total? Explica por qué importa la cantidad de lados.
hintsEs: Ambos polígonos usan triángulos idénticos (base 6 pies, altura 5 pies): solo cambia el NÚMERO de triángulos.
Halla el área de un triángulo con ½ × 6 × 5 y luego multiplica por 6 para el hexágono y por 5 para el pentágono.
Calcula ½ × 6 × 5 para un triángulo. Luego compara 6 copias con 5 copias y explica por qué importa la cantidad.

extending.hint: Run the area formula backward: total area = number of triangles × ½ × base × height. Fill in what you know, then solve for the missing factor.
hints: Write the equation for the row before you compute anything: total = n × (½ × b × h).
Hexagon row: 6 × (½ × 9 × h) = 216 simplifies to 27h = 216, so divide.
The octagon row is different — the unknown is the triangle COUNT: n × (½ × 4 × 5) = 80 becomes 10n = 80.
extending.explanation: Each row runs the formula in reverse. Hexagon: 6 × (½ × 9 × h) = 27h = 216, so h = 8 ft. Pentagon: 5 × (½ × b × 6) = 15b = 180, so b = 12 ft. Octagon: n × (½ × 4 × 5) = 10n = 80, so n = 8 triangles — which checks out, since an octagon has 8 sides. Decagon: 10 × (½ × 3 × h) = 15h = 60, so h = 4 ft.
extending.explanationEs: Cada fila usa la fórmula al revés. Hexágono: 6 × (½ × 9 × h) = 27h = 216, así que h = 8 pies. Pentágono: 5 × (½ × b × 6) = 15b = 180, así que b = 12 pies. Octágono: n × (½ × 4 × 5) = 10n = 80, así que n = 8 triángulos, lo cual concuerda porque un octágono tiene 8 lados. Decágono: 10 × (½ × 3 × h) = 15h = 60, así que h = 4 pies.
hintsEs: Escribe la ecuación de la fila antes de calcular: total = n × (½ × b × h).
Fila del hexágono: 6 × (½ × 9 × h) = 216 se simplifica a 27h = 216, así que divide.
La fila del octágono es distinta: la incógnita es la CANTIDAD de triángulos. n × (½ × 4 × 5) = 80 se convierte en 10n = 80.

connect.scenario: The parks department hired your firm to finish a regular octagonal gazebo at the center of Patterson Park. Seen from above, the gazebo floor decomposes into 8 congruent triangles that meet at the center point, and each triangle has a base of 5 feet and a height of 6 feet. The flooring contractor charges $3 per square foot and needs a total price before Friday's budget meeting.

connect.promptQuestion: How much will the gazebo flooring cost?
connect.prompt: One triangle's area is ___ sq ft. The octagon has ___ triangles, so total area = ___ sq ft. The cost is ___ x $3 = $___.

check.stem: What is the area of one center triangle?
check.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 sq ft.

check.stem: What is the total floor area of the octagon?
check.explanation: The octagon is made of 8 identical triangles: 8 × 15 = 120 sq ft.

connect.modelAnswer: Each of the 8 center triangles has area ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 sq ft, so the octagon covers 8 × 15 = 120 sq ft. At $3 per square foot the flooring costs 120 × $3 = $360.

exitTicket.stem: A regular pentagon is decomposed into 5 triangles from its center. Each triangle has a base of 7 inches and a height of 4.8 inches. What is the total area of the pentagon?
exitTicket.explanation: One triangle: A = 1/2 x 7 x 4.8 = 16.8 sq in. Total = 5 x 16.8 = 84 square inches.
choiceFeedback: That's one triangle — multiply by all 5 triangles.
You skipped the ½ — each triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8.
Right value, wrong unit — area is square inches.
hints: Two steps hide in this problem: one triangle's area first, then all 5 triangles together.
One triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8; the pentagon is 5 of those. Skipping either step leads to a wrong path.
Take half of 7 × 4.8 to get one triangle's area, then multiply that by the 5 triangles.

choices: The base is always twice the height
A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
We always divide area formulas by 2
questions.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.
